taxon_scope: 35 Cirsium taxa; focal C. brevicaule included
design: 1988-1998 multi-taxon flower-head collection and insect rearing survey; attack rate = emerged insects / collected flower heads x100
interaction_axis: flower-head antagonist regime x host phenology x geography
quantitative_result: C. brevicaule: 837 flower heads, 3 effective samples, Larinus latissimus emerged from all 3 Okinawa samples, mean AR=26.1; C. japonicum L. latissimus mean AR=1.1. L. meleagris mainly autumn hosts; Xyphosia punctigera concentrated on Japan Sea side and Urophora sachalinensis mainly Pacific side.
chapter2_role: direct East-Asian/focal-taxon evidence that flower-head antagonist exposure exists and is phenology/geography structured
transport_boundary: Does not estimate seed-fitness loss, selection on a capitulum trait, or white-vs-coloured contrast; AR is emergence per 100 heads and may exceed 100.
source_title: Faunal make-up, host range and infestation rate of weevils and tephritid flies associated with flower heads of the thistle Cirsium (Cardueae: Asteraceae) in Japan

design: two-population field observational study linking flower production, predispersal seed predation and annual seed production
quantitative_result: At both sites predation increased with flower/head production. Nikko: 90.8% of heads infested; estimated seed predation probability 25.3%; among 13 plants seed damage 7.9-51.5%; predator number vs damaged-seed proportion r2=0.48 P=0.001; saturating damage-vs-floret relationship r2=0.44 P=0.013.
chapter2_role: direct Japanese Cirsium evidence that display benefit can be opposed by predispersal seed-predator cost
transport_boundary: Observational, not antagonist-reduction experiment; cannot enter the pooled experimental RR=2.674 effect size and does not identify one head-architecture trait as causal.
source_title: Effects of flower production and predispersal seed predation on reproduction in Cirsium purpuratum
